subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Karl Benz and the First Car
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Karl Benz and the First Car.

hook.text: Karl Benz filed a patent for a motorized vehicle in 1886. The world barely noticed.

buildup.text: His Patent-Motorwagen had three wheels, a single cylinder, and a top speed of 10 mph.

discovery.text: Benz wasn't just an inventor—he built the entire car: engine, frame, ignition, and steering.

twist.text: His investors wanted him to focus on stationary engines. Cars seemed like expensive toys.

climax.text: It took Bertha Benz's cross-country drive to prove the car had a future beyond the workshop.

punchline.text: The first carmaker needed his wife to prove his car.

quiz.question: How fast could the first Benz car go?

details.summary: Karl Benz patented the first gasoline-powered automobile in 1886, a three-wheeled vehicle called the Patent-Motorwagen that proved self-propelled transport was practical and commercially viable.
details.whyItMatters: Benz's invention launched the entire automotive industry. His patent number 37435 is recognized as the birth certificate of the automobile, sparking over a century of transportation evolution.
takeaways: Benz received his patent on January 29, 1886
The Motorwagen had a single-cylinder engine producing 0.75 HP
His wife Bertha proved the car's viability on a 65-mile journey

faq.question: Did Karl Benz invent the car all by himself?
faq.answer: Benz built the first purpose-designed automobile, but Gottlieb Daimler independently developed a gasoline engine at the same time. Both men are credited as fathers of the modern automobile.

faq.question: Why was Bertha Benz's journey important?
faq.answer: Her 1888 trip from Mannheim to Pforzheim was the first long-distance car journey. It proved the automobile could travel meaningful distances and generated publicity that helped convince skeptical buyers.
